title: BIASX: “Thinking Slow” in Toxic Content Moderation with Explanations of Implied Social Biases

bias_targets.methodology: Crowdsourced human evaluation measuring how free-text explanations of implied stereotypes affect content moderators' accuracy in detecting subtly sexist posts.
Crowdsourced human evaluation measuring how free-text explanations of implied stereotypes affect content moderators' accuracy in detecting anti-transgender statements.

Crowdsourced human evaluation measuring how free-text explanations of implied stereotypes affect content moderators' accuracy in detecting subtly racist statements (e.g., targeting Black or Indian people).
Crowdsourced human evaluation measuring how free-text explanations of implied stereotypes affect content moderators' accuracy in detecting homophobic or biphobic language.
Crowdsourced human evaluation measuring how free-text explanations of implied stereotypes affect content moderators' accuracy in detecting Islamophobic and anti-Semitic statements.

Crowdsourced human evaluation measuring how free-text explanations of implied stereotypes affect content moderators' accuracy in detecting xenophobic or national stereotypes (e.g., targeting Brazilians, Americans, or Japanese).

Crowdsourced human evaluation measuring how free-text explanations of implied stereotypes affect content moderators' accuracy in detecting specific regional stereotypes (e.g., targeting people from Alabama).
